name: Infrastructure Verification
description: Approved host: certificate baseline and a few selected ports at a low rate; reconcile what you found against what you expected to own.
legal_notes: Only for assets you own or hold written authorization to test. This workflow never sends a request itself: it reads authorization and observation records, and a person creates, approves and starts every exact plan in the Verification workspace. Findings are observations to verify, not proof of compromise.
quota_note: No network requests (works on local data)
example_output: An inventory delta: ports and certificates observed against the authorization, with notes about what is uncertain.
capability_gaps: This workflow is manual only and cannot send requests: checks run from the Verification workspace after a person approves the exact plan.
Not verified against third-party sites: every check was exercised against local lab servers only.
Nmap and Naabu are optional and used only if installed and version-verified; the built-in connect check always works.
instructions: Approved host: certificate baseline and a few selected ports at a low rate; reconcile what you found against what you expected to own.

definition.name: Infrastructure Verification
definition.description: Approved host: certificate baseline and a few selected ports at a low rate; reconcile what you found against what you expected to own.

config.prompt: Confirm you own the asset or hold written authorization to test it, and that the authorization names the host, ports and checks. Consent from a person is not authorization for their domains.
Open Verification. Create a plan for the authorized host: a TLS handshake and a connect check of at most 10 listed ports (optionally Nmap or Naabu if installed). Approve the exact plan and start it.
Compare open ports and certificates with your asset inventory. Note anything you did not expect, and record what you could not determine.
